decision_table.name: Determine_DC_Filing_Requirement
decision_table.description: Determine if corporation must file DC franchise tax return. Checks for physical presence or economic nexus.

condition.name: has_physical_presence
condition.comment: Has physical presence in DC (office, employees, property)

actions.action: // Physical nexus established - filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
DC franchise tax filing required due to physical presence (office, employees, or property in District).
Every corporation or financial institution must file DC Form D-20 if it carries on or engages in any trade, business, or commercial activity in DC or receives income from DC sources.
Reference: DC Code § 47-1807.02 (Tax on corporations) Reference: DC Code § 47-1805.02a (Definition of doing business) Reference: DC Form D-20 Instructions (Corporation Franchise Tax Return) Reference: DC OTR Tax Guide: Nexus (https://otr.cfo.dc.gov)

DC franchise tax filing required due to economic nexus (post-Wayfair). Threshold: $100,000 gross receipts OR 200 transactions
DC maintains relatively low economic nexus thresholds, making it easier for remote sellers to trigger registration obligations. Additionally, there is no minimum dollar threshold for income purposes - even $1 of DC-sourced revenue creates a filing obligation.
Reference: South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018) Reference: DC OTR Economic Nexus Guidance Reference: DC Code § 47-1810.02 (Allocation and apportionment)
No DC nexus - no filing requirement. Any estimated payments would be refunded.

decision_table.name: Calculate_DC_Income_Adjustments
decision_table.description: Calculate DC state-specific additions and subtractions to federal taxable income.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to calculate adjustments

rule.policy:
DC state-specific income adjustments to federal taxable income.
Additions may include: - Interest on U.S. government obligations (DC Code § 47-1803.02(a)(2)) - IRC Section 199A deduction addback (DC decouples) - Bonus depreciation addback (DC Code § 47-1803.03(a)(4)(A)) - State income taxes deducted on federal return - Foreign dividends received deduction (certain types)
Subtractions may include: - Interest on DC and other state/municipal obligations (DC Code § 47-1803.02(a)(2)) - Qualified High Technology Company (QHTC) income deductions - DC net operating loss carryforward (5-year limit, DC Code § 47-1803.03(a)(10)) - Foreign source income (under certain conditions)
Reference: DC Form D-20 Schedule UB (Unincorporated Business adjustments apply similarly) Reference: DC Code § 47-1803.02 (Definition of gross income) Reference: DC Code § 47-1803.03 (Deductions) Reference: DC Code § 47-1817.01 (Qualified High Technology Companies) Reference: DC Form D-20 Instructions
No nexus - no state adjustments calculated.

decision_table.name: Calculate_DC_State_Tax
decision_table.description: Calculate DC corporate franchise tax. Applies 8.25% flat rate to apportioned and adjusted taxable income.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to owe tax

rule.policy:
DC corporate franchise tax calculation:
1. Federal taxable income: [Form 1120 line 28] 2. Apportioned to DC: × [Apportionment % using single-sales factor] 3. State additions: + [Additions from Schedule UB] 4. State subtractions: - [Subtractions from Schedule UB] 5. DC taxable income: = [Result] 6. DC tax rate: × 8.25% 7. DC income-based tax: = [Tax before credits] 8. DC credits: - [Credits] 9. DC tax (before minimum): = [Income-based tax]
DC uses 100% single-sales factor apportionment with market-based sourcing. Tax rate is a flat 8.25% with no brackets or alternative minimum tax.
DC franchise tax is the GREATER of: - Income-based tax (calculated above), OR - Minimum tax ($250 if DC gross receipts <= $1M, $1,000 if > $1M)
Available DC credits include: - Research and Development Tax Credit - Job Growth Tax Credit - Historic Homebuyer Tax Credit - Low Income Housing Tax Credit - Renewable Energy Tax Credit - Arts and Humanities Tax Credit
Reference: DC Form D-20 (Corporation Franchise Tax Return) Instructions Reference: DC Code § 47-1807.02 (8.25% tax rate) Reference: DC Code § 47-1810.02 (Apportionment - single-sales factor since 2015) Reference: DC Code § 47-1807.06 (Minimum tax) Reference: DC OTR Corporate Franchise Tax Publications
No DC nexus - no tax liability. Any estimated payments are refunded.

No DC taxable income - no income-based tax liability. However, DC minimum tax still applies based on gross receipts (calculated in table 55090).
DC allows NOL carryforward for 5 years (DC Code § 47-1803.03(a)(10)). This differs from federal NOL rules which allow longer carryforward periods.

decision_table.name: Calculate_DC_Minimum_Tax
decision_table.description: Calculate DC minimum franchise tax based on gross receipts. Final tax is greater of income-based tax or minimum tax.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to owe minimum tax

rule.policy:
DC minimum franchise tax: $1,000 (gross receipts exceed $1 million)
DC franchise tax is the GREATER of: - Income-based tax calculated at 8.25% rate, OR - Minimum tax of $1,000
This ensures corporations with significant DC activity pay at least a minimum amount even if they report losses or minimal taxable income.
Reference: DC Code § 47-1807.06 (Minimum tax) Reference: DC Form D-20 Instructions Reference: DC OTR Franchise Tax FAQs

DC minimum franchise tax: $250 (gross receipts $1 million or less)
DC franchise tax is the GREATER of: - Income-based tax calculated at 8.25% rate, OR - Minimum tax of $250
This minimum tax applies even to smaller corporations with DC nexus, ensuring all entities with DC activity contribute to District revenue.
Reference: DC Code § 47-1807.06 (Minimum tax) Reference: DC Form D-20 Instructions Reference: DC OTR Franchise Tax FAQs
No DC nexus - no minimum tax requirement.
